newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Cypriot leader says missile crisis not over.
newsitem.headline: Turk Cypriot leader says missile crisis not over.

text.p: Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash said on Tuesday the crisis over the deployment of anti-aircraft missiles in Cyprus was not over, contrary to the view of a U.S. envoy, Turkey's Anatolian news agency reported.

Asked if the missile crisis was continuing, Denktash said: "of course its continuing...(Cypriot President Glafcos) Clerides has neither made a sacrifice nor a gesture. So what is going to happen after 16 months?"
Denktash was speaking at Ercan airport in the Turkish Cypriot north of the island after the departure of the Turkish armed forces chief General Ismail Hakki Karadayi.

Karadayi's visit marked a further show of support for the breakaway Turkish Cypriot state by Turkey, which last week threatened to destroy a Russian-made S-300 missile system which Cyprus is planning to install.
U.S. envoy Carey Cavanaugh earlier said the planned missile deployment was no longer a crisis because the Cyrpus government assured him it would not import the system for at least 16 months.
Cavanaugh also said agreement was close on a military accord to reduce tension along the ceasefire line dividing Greek and Turkish Cypriots.

The Cypriot government dismissed as a "misunderstanding" his reference to U.N. proposals relating to the unloading of live ammunition among troops on either side of the 180-km (110-mile) ceasefire line and unmanning sentry posts.

"There has not been any agreement other than that which was already in place, that the military dialogue would continue based on what is stipulated in the relevant resolution of the United Nations," Clerides told reporters.
Turkey invaded Cyprus in 1974 in response to a shortlived coup in Nicosia engineered by the military then ruling Greece.

Turkey's invasion resulted in the island's division and establishment of a breakaway Turkish Cypriot state in the north recognised only by Ankara. About 30,000 Turkish troops are still stationed in Cyprus.
